news.headline: Delhi High Court Reprimands SSC Over Rigid Interpretation of Eligibility Criteria for Nursing Posts
news.story_lead: The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition filed by the Staff Selection Commission against a Central Administrative Tribunal order, ruling that qualified medical professionals should not be disqualified due to narrow and overly restrictive interpretations of eligibility rules. The court urged public recruiting bodies to adopt a pragmatic approach when evaluating candidate qualifications.
news.full_article_text:
The Delhi High Court criticized the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) for adopting a legally unsustainable and overly myopic perspective in rejecting the job application of a qualified candidate for a nursing officer (allopathic) post. A division bench comprising Justice C. Hari Shankar and Justice Nivedita Anil Sharma delivered the ruling while upholding an order issued by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT).

The dispute originated from a recruitment advertisement published in January 2024 for nursing officer positions. The applicant, who held a post-basic BSc nursing qualification, had her candidature rejected by the SSC on the grounds that her post-qualification registration date fell after the prescribed cut-off deadline. The candidate subsequently challenged this rejection before the CAT.

On January 29, the Central Administrative Tribunal ruled in favor of the applicant, observing that she had already been registered as a certified nurse by the Delhi Nursing Council in 2018, prior to the cut-off date. Unwilling to accept the CAT ruling, the SSC appealed to the Delhi High Court, contending that the 2018 registration certificate could not be considered valid for the post since it preceded her acquiring the requisite post-basic BSc nursing degree specified in the job advertisement.

Dismissing the SSC's challenge, the High Court emphasized that professional doctors and nurses serve as vital assets to society. The bench remarked that recruiting bodies ought not to throw out genuine, qualified applicants by enforcing hyper-technical or rigid interpretations of qualification norms. The court expressed disappointment over the SSC's decision to litigate the matter rather than graciously accepting the tribunal's direction, and ordered the commission to comply with the CAT's ruling within four weeks.
news.background_context: The recruitment notification for the post of nursing officer (allopathic) was released by the recruitment agency in January 2024. Following the rejection of her application due to cut-off date interpretations, the candidate approached the Central Administrative Tribunal, which decided in her favour on January 29.

The case involved the rejection of a candidate's application for a nursing officer (allopathic) position advertised in January 2024.
SSC rejected the application claiming the candidate obtained registration after the prescribed cut-off date.
CAT ruled in the candidate's favour on January 29, pointing out her existing 2018 registration with the Delhi Nursing Council.
SSC argued in court that the 2018 registration preceded the candidate's post-basic BSc nursing qualification.
A bench of Justice C. Hari Shankar and Justice Nivedita Anil Sharma termed the SSC's stance legally unsustainable and overly myopic.
The High Court highlighted that qualified doctors and nurses are public assets who should not be excluded due to rigid interpretations.
The court directed the SSC to implement the CAT order within four weeks.

exam_relevance: Relevant for Polity and Governance topics regarding public service recruitment standards, administrative tribunal functions, and judicial review of executive/recruitment agency decisions.
Illustrates judicial oversight over administrative agencies (SSC) to ensure fair play and public interest in public employment.
news.upsc_analysis: The Delhi High Court's ruling reinforces the legal principle of proportionality and purposive interpretation in public employment disputes. Administrative bodies often adopt rigid, hyper-technical interpretations of eligibility criteria, leading to unnecessary litigation and public resource wastage. By emphasizing that qualified professionals like nurses and doctors are social assets, the judiciary underscores that administrative procedures must serve the primary objective of recruiting competent personnel rather than arbitrarily excluding eligible candidates on procedural technicalities.

SSC challenged the Central Administrative Tribunal's order in the High Court instead of implementing the tribunal's decision.
impacts: Reaffirmation of candidate-friendly, practical interpretations of qualification norms in public service recruitments.
Directive to the SSC to comply with the tribunal's directive to consider the candidate within four weeks.
Judicial precedent discouraging administrative bodies from engaging in pedantic litigation against qualified applicants.

Increased burden on judicial and tribunal systems due to appeals against reasonable administrative decisions.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 14 (Right to Equality) and Article 16 (Equality of Opportunity in matters of Public Employment) of the Indian Constitution, which prevent arbitrary rejection of candidates in public recruitment processes.
way_forward: Recruiting agencies such as the SSC should issue clear, non-ambiguous eligibility guidelines in recruitment notifications.
Public bodies should accept tribunal orders graciously when public interest and fairness are upheld, avoiding avoidable court challenges.

- Key issue: SSC's rejection of a qualified nursing officer applicant based on literal interpretation of cut-off dates.
- High Court stance: Public recruiting authorities must refrain from 'legally unsustainable and unnecessarily myopic' views.
- Legal doctrine: Purposive interpretation of eligibility criteria over hyper-technical procedural grounds to protect public interest and fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 16.

दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय ने नर्सिंग अधिकारी (अलोपैथिक) पद के लिए एक योग्य उम्मीदवार के नौकरी आवेदन को खारिज करने पर कर्मचारी चयन आयोग (SSC) के दृष्टिकोण को कानूनी रूप से अनुचित और अत्यधिक अदूरदर्शी बताया। न्यायमूर्ति सी. हरि शंकर और न्यायमूर्ति निवेदिता अनिल शर्मा की पीठ ने केंद्रीय प्रशासनिक न्यायाधिकरण (CAT) द्वारा दिए गए आदेश को बरकरार रखते हुए यह फैसला सुनाया।

यह विवाद जनवरी 2024 में प्रकाशित नर्सिंग अधिकारी पदों की भर्ती अधिसूचना से शुरू हुआ था। पोस्ट-बेसिक बीएससी नर्सिंग योग्यता रखने वाली एक महिला उम्मीदवार का आवेदन SSC ने इस आधार पर खारिज कर दिया था कि उसकी योग्यता के बाद की पंजीकरण तिथि निर्धारित कट-ऑफ तिथि के बाद की थी। उम्मीदवार ने इस अस्वीकृति को CAT के समक्ष चुनौती दी।

29 जनवरी को, केंद्रीय प्रशासनिक न्यायाधिकरण ने उम्मीदवार के पक्ष में फैसला सुनाया और कहा कि वह कट-ऑफ तिथि से पहले 2018 में ही दिल्ली नर्सिंग काउंसिल द्वारा एक नर्स के रूप में पंजीकृत हो चुकी थी। SSC ने इस फैसले को स्वीकार करने के बजाय दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय में चुनौती दी और तर्क दिया कि 2018 के पंजीकरण प्रमाण पत्र पर विचार नहीं किया जा सकता क्योंकि यह विज्ञापन में निर्धारित बीएससी योग्यता प्राप्त करने से पहले जारी किया गया था।

उच्च न्यायालय ने SSC की याचिका को खारिज करते हुए कहा कि योग्य डॉक्टर और नर्स समाज के लिए महत्वपूर्ण संपत्ति हैं। पीठ ने टिप्पणी की कि भर्ती संस्थाओं को योग्यता मानदंडों की अति-तकनीकी या कठोर व्याख्या अपनाकर वास्तविक, योग्य आवेदकों को बाहर नहीं करना चाहिए। अदालत ने SSC को चार सप्ताह के भीतर CAT के आदेश का पालन करने का निर्देश दिया।

SSC को चार सप्ताह के भीतर CAT के आदेश को लागू करने का निर्देश दिया गया।

news.headline: Tragic Fire in Arunachal’s Kurung Kumey Kills Four and Destroys 25 Homes
news.story_lead: A major fire broke out in Parsi Parlo town of Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey district, claiming four lives, including three children and a woman. The blaze destroyed 25 residential houses, leaving several families displaced and exposing serious gaps in the remote district's firefighting preparedness.
news.full_article_text:
A devastating fire struck Parsi Parlo town in the Kurung Kumey district of Arunachal Pradesh early Thursday morning around 2:00 AM. The rapid spread of the blaze through the residential area led to the deaths of four people, comprising three children and one woman, while completely gutting 25 houses along with personal belongings.

Preliminary investigations by local police indicate that the fire is suspected to have started in a kitchen, although official enquiries are ongoing to confirm the exact cause. Official confirmation regarding the identities of the victims and the full extent of financial loss is awaited.

The disaster has drawn critical attention to the lack of basic firefighting infrastructure in the region. Parsi Parlo does not have its own fire station. Furthermore, a fire tender sent from Koloriang failed to reach the incident site on time due to its dilapidated condition, severely impeding efforts to control the flames before they engulfed the neighborhood.

In response to the tragedy, Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu expressed sorrow over the loss of life and destruction, directing local authorities to deliver all necessary relief to affected households. Additionally, the All Nyishi Youth Association (ANYA), headed by President Jamru Ruja, called for urgent government rehabilitation measures and announced a community donation drive to support the victims.

hindi_translation.headline: अरुणाचल के कुरुंग कुमे में भीषण आग से चार लोगों की मौत, 25 घर जलकर खाक
hindi_translation.story_lead: अरुणाचल प्रदेश के कुरुंग कुमे जिले के पारसी पारलो कस्बे में तड़के भीषण आग लगने से एक महिला और तीन बच्चों समेत चार लोगों की मौत हो गई। इस हादसे में 25 घर जलकर नष्ट हो गए, जिससे कई परिवार बेघर हो गए और क्षेत्र की अग्निशमन व्यवस्था की खामियां उजागर हुईं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
अरुणाचल प्रदेश के कुरुंग कुमे जिले में स्थित पारसी पारलो कस्बे में गुरुवार तड़के लगभग 2:00 बजे भीषण आग लग गई। आवासीय क्षेत्र में आग तेजी से फैलने के कारण तीन बच्चों और एक महिला सहित चार लोगों की जान चली गई, जबकि कम से कम 25 घर और घरेलू सामान पूरी तरह से जलकर खाक हो गए।

स्थानीय पुलिस के अनुसार, शुरुआती जांच में आग लगने का कारण रसोईघर माना जा रहा है, हालांकि सटीक कारणों की जांच जारी है। मृतकों की आधिकारिक पहचान और संपत्ति के नुकसान के पूरे आकलन की पुष्टि होना अभी बाकी है।

इस त्रासदी ने दुर्गम जिले में अग्निशमन बुनियादी ढांचे की कमी को उजागर किया है। पारसी पारलो में कोई फायर स्टेशन नहीं है, और पास के कोलोरिएंग से भेजा गया अग्निशमन वाहन जर्जर स्थिति के कारण समय पर घटनास्थल नहीं पहुंच सका। समय पर मदद न मिलने से आग पर काबू पाने के प्रयासों में बाधा आई और आग पूरे इलाके में फैल गई।

इस घटना पर दुख व्यक्त करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री पेमा खांडू ने प्रभावित परिवारों को सभी आवश्यक राहत सामग्री और सहायता प्रदान करने के निर्देश दिए। इसके अलावा, ऑल निशि यूथ एसोसिएशन (ANYA) के अध्यक्ष जम्रू रुजा ने पीड़ित परिवारों के प्रति संवेदना व्यक्त की, तत्काल राहत और पुनर्वास की मांग की तथा सहायता के लिए एक सामुदायिक दान अभियान आयोजित करने की घोषणा की।

news.headline: 36-Year-Old Man Dies by Suicide at Kanpur Mall Following Dispute Over Marriage Proposal
news.story_lead: A 36-year-old man working in Saudi Arabia died after jumping from the second floor of Rave Moti Mall in Kanpur's Sarvodaya Nagar area on Wednesday evening. The incident occurred after an argument broke out when his partner of ten years turned down his marriage proposal. Police have sent the body for a post-mortem examination and are awaiting a formal complaint.
news.full_article_text:
A 36-year-old man, identified as Imtiyaz Riyaz alias Sikandar, died after leaping from the second floor of a commercial complex in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The event occurred on Wednesday evening at Rave Moti Mall, situated in the Sarvodaya Nagar locality.

According to police reports, Sikandar had been employed in Saudi Arabia and had been in a relationship with the woman—a relative's daughter—for nearly ten years with the intention of marrying her. However, officials stated that she had reportedly become involved with another person during his absence abroad.

On the evening of the incident, Sikandar arrived at the shopping mall accompanied by two acquaintances and summoned the woman to discuss their relationship. Following a heated argument during which she declined his proposal of marriage, Sikandar jumped from the second floor of the building. Authorities were alerted and reached the scene at approximately 8:00 PM. He was immediately transported to Regency Hospital, where medical personnel declared him dead upon arrival.

Assistant Commissioner of Police (Swaroop Nagar) Jyoti Shri confirmed that officers inspected the premises and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Police stated that further legal proceedings will be initiated upon receipt of a formal complaint.

news.story_lead: Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026 - Published 6 hours ago Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free. news.full_article_text: Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026 - Published 6 hours ago Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free. It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi. He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died. Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation. "Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak. "This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X. - What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? Published 15 September Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October. All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission. Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers. Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday. Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over. The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown. Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries. Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams. The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country. In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens. Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings. The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries. Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June. But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE. The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures. Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August. news.headline: Gurugram bans coal, wood-fired tandoors at hotels and eateries under revised GRAP norms to curb pollution
news.story_lead: Gurugram bans coal, wood-fired tandoors at hotels and eateries under revised GRAP norms to curb pollution Under the revised provisions of the GRAP issued by the CAQM, only equipment powered by electricity, gas, or other approved clean fuels may now be used. District Magistrate and Gurugram Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh has issued orders to prohibit the use of coal and wood as fuel in tandoors at all hotels, restaurants, and open-air eateries across the district in an effort to combat air pollution. Under the revised provisions of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), only equipment powered by electricity, gas, or other approved clean fuels may now be used in these establishments.

news.story_lead: These children had to leave their primary school in Rome as a result of one of the threats sent on Wednesday - Published 11 November 2026, 12:30 GMT Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities. news.full_article_text: These children had to leave their primary school in Rome as a result of one of the threats sent on Wednesday - Published 11 November 2026, 12:30 GMT Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities. In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger". "These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook. Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected. "As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said. Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated. "Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said. Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected. The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools. The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project. Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals. Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings. - No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister Published 1 hour ago - Police treating threatening email sent to more than 300 schools as 'hoax' Published 3 hours ago On Wednesday one Milan headteacher, Anna Bertato, told Italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "It was already classified as spam by a student at a university in Taiwan." Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in. "The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh." Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home. Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports. In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report". news.headline: RBI issues domestic transfer norms; walk-in customers can send up to ₹50k
news.story_lead: RBI issues domestic transfer norms; walk-in customers can send up to ₹50k The framework for Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) was introduced in order to facilitate small-value fund transfers through formal banking channels. Walk-in customers at bank branches can utilise the cash pay-in service to remit funds up to ₹ 50,000 directly to a beneficiary's bank account through NEFT, the Reserve Bank said on Wednesday. With a view to harmonising and consolidating the extant instructions relating to Domestic Money Transfer (DMT), the central bank has issued the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026.
news.full_article_text: RBI issues domestic transfer norms; walk-in customers can send up to ₹50k The framework for Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) was introduced in order to facilitate small-value fund transfers through formal banking channels. Walk-in customers at bank branches can utilise the cash pay-in service to remit funds up to ₹ 50,000 directly to a beneficiary's bank account through NEFT, the Reserve Bank said on Wednesday. With a view to harmonising and consolidating the extant instructions relating to Domestic Money Transfer (DMT), the central bank has issued the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026. The framework for Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) was introduced in order to facilitate small-value fund transfers through formal banking channels, particularly for persons, including migrant workers, who lack access to such channels due to lack of proof of identity/address. "A walk-in customer at a bank branch can remit funds up to ₹ 50,000 to the bank account of a beneficiary through NEFT," said the RBI's latest Directions, which came into effect from Wednesday. Banks are also permitted to allow such customers to transfer funds to a bank account of a beneficiary through Business Correspondents (BCs) and ATMs up to a maximum amount of ₹ 5,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of ₹ 25,000 per remitter. RBI further said banks are permitted to provide services, which facilitate transfer of funds from the accounts of their customers for delivery in cash to the recipients not having bank accounts at an ATM or through an agent appointed as Business Correspondent, or through any other authorised payment channels. On payment of amounts transferred from a bank account (Cash Pay-out Service), banks are permitted to provide services which facilitate transfer of funds from the accounts of their customers for delivery in cash to the recipients not having bank accounts at an ATM or through an agent appointed as Business Correspondent, or through any other authorised payment channels. "The maximum amount that may be transferred under the Cash Pay-out Service shall be ₹ 10,000 per transaction, subject to an overall monthly ceiling of ₹ 25,000 per beneficiary," the RBI said. Card-to-card transfers are excluded from the purview of the Directions. RBI further said banks and non-banks should put in place robust systems of safeguards, including velocity checks and alerts to customers regarding credits into accounts using the facilities provided under the Directions. "Any unusual spurt in the volume of credits in a particular account or group of accounts shall be investigated immediately," it said, and added appropriate authorities should be alerted regarding suspicious transactions. Fund transfers under the facility are expected to be effected on a real-time or near real-time basis, the Reserve Bank said.
